title: Clamp two boards together with a one-hand bar clamp by pumping its trigger
instruction: Clamp the two boards together edge to edge with the bar clamp so that the joint stays closed, then let go.
context: A one-hand bar clamp is the clamp of home workshops and repairs: whoever has glued a chair rung, a drawer front or a split board has held the pieces together with one while the glue set. Its jaws are put round the work and the trigger is squeezed stroke by stroke; each stroke draws the bar a few millimetres through the grip, until the joint is closed and pressed, and the clamp then holds the force by itself. Pushing the bar shut by hand closes the jaws but leaves no force on the work: only the trigger does. The task is done when the clamp, let go, still presses the two boards together.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases (x away from the arms, y to the left); heights over the bench top. One fixed layout, nothing varies by seed. Two pine boards, 200 x 60 x 18 mm, 110 g each, lying flat side by side with their long axes along x, near ends at x 33, their long edges 2 mm apart, the pair's middle at y -6. In front of them, lying flat, an IRWIN QUICK-GRIP one-handed mini bar clamp, 6 in (opening 152 mm, throat 62 mm, rated 140 lb; about 0.3 kg): its steel bar along y, both jaws pointing away from the arms and opened 14 cm, their tips at x 31, 2 cm short of the boards' near ends; the pad of the grip's jaw 5 mm outside the right board's outer edge, the pad of the bar's jaw 13 mm outside the left board's; the grip's head at x 24.8, y -15.7, its handle pointing towards the arms, the yellow trigger along the handle's right side, open. Nothing else is on the bench. Both arms start in their ready pose; the clamp lies nearer the right arm.
scoring: By where things are at the end of the trial. Round the boards: both pads' middles 1 cm or more inside the boards' ends and within their thickness, each pad on its board's outer side. Closed: round the boards, and the joint between the boards and both gaps between pad and board 0.5 mm or less, at both ends of the joint. Clamped: closed, with 20 N or more between the grip's pad and the board. 0.25: round the boards. 0.5: closed, under 20 N. 0.75: clamped. 1.0: clamped, the boards' near ends within 3 mm of each other and their tops level within 1 mm, everything at rest and both grippers 3 cm or more from clamp and boards; held for 1 s the trial ends as a success. 0 otherwise, or if a part has left the bench. Real bench: a thin load cell or force-sensing film (0 to 200 N, 3 mm or less) between the grip's pad and the board reads 20 N or more after the hands are clear; a 0.5 mm feeler gauge for the joint and the pad gaps; a straightedge and a tape for the rest; the video for the release.
reset_notes: Press the clamp's release lever, open the jaws to 14 cm and lay the clamp back on its marks; lay the boards back side by side 2 mm apart. If a force film is used, tape it to the grip's pad before the trial.
fidelity: Rigid bodies in PhysX. The clamp is built from its parts: a grip with one jaw, a bar on a slide through the grip with the other jaw, a trigger on a pin with a spring (assumed; read in the scene with a known load 4 cm from the pin: 7.7 N start to close it, 10.4 N hold it closed). The drive and lock plates, which on the real clamp grip the bar by tilting, are stops moved every control step: squeezed, the trigger draws the bar 5.9 mm a stroke; the bar cannot go back; pushed by hand it slides closed freely and keeps no force when the hand lets go. The clamping force is read from a sprung pad on the grip's jaw (1 mm for every 40 N, assumed, standing for the give of pads, jaws and bar), not from contact forces. With the gripper's 50 N on the trigger the clamp reaches 137 to 150 N here; the real one is rated 140 lb (623 N). The trigger's lever arm inside the grip (15 mm) is chosen, not measured: with a shorter arm the boards sank into each other from about 150 N. Pad and trigger move with more inertia than their real 10 g and 25 g, because a light body pressed between a hand and joints gives way in this simulator; their weight is the real one. Sizes other than the listed opening, throat and rating are assumed and to be measured; friction: pine on the bench 0.30, pine on pine 0.25, rubber 0.8 (assumed).
